title: artifact host policy: a tracking server connects only to the host of its default artifact root or artifacts destination for host-addressed URIs, unless the scheme is listed in MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES
answers: Why does creating an experiment with an ftp, sftp or hdfs artifact_location return a 400 on my tracking server?
How do I allow a second HDFS namenode or SFTP host for experiment or workspace artifact storage?
Where is the check that stops the server from connecting to arbitrary hosts for model version sources and run artifacts?
Why does a job or runs:/ download fail with 'does not connect to artifact location'?
body:
Path: Any artifact location a client supplies or the server has stored and then connects to: experiment artifact_location, workspace default_artifact_root and trace archival location, model version source, and stored run, model version, logged model and trace locations on fetch. Host-addressed schemes (ftp, sftp, hdfs, viewfs, http, https, mlflow-artifacts, r2, b2, abfss) go through mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:rejected_host_addressed_scheme. Checked at acceptance in mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_artifact_uri_scheme, at fetch in mlflow/server/handlers.py:_get_artifact_repository_for_uri, and in every server-process repository build in mlflow/store/artifact/artifact_repository_registry.py:ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository.
Rule: A host-addressed URI is accepted only if its (scheme family, hostname, effective port) matches a target derived from the server's _MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_ROOT or _MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_DESTINATION env marker (mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:host_addressed_uri_targets), or its scheme is in mlflow/environment_variables.py:MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES. Ports default to the scheme's well-known port, hostless ftp/sftp/hdfs count as host-addressed, and an authority containing a backslash or whitespace is never trusted. Registry enforcement runs only when host_policy.py:is_tracking_server_process() is true, so client processes are unaffected. Any new server code that builds an artifact repository from a client-supplied or stored URI should go through the registry or _get_artifact_repository_for_uri. The marker strings are duplicated from mlflow/server/constants.py and must stay equal to them.
Symptom: A client could set an experiment artifact_location or model version source to an arbitrary host, and the server would open a connection to it (SSRF, CWE-918, GHSA-mr9f-g8qf-4w4j). After the fix the same request gets a 400 naming the field, or the stored location fails at fetch time.
Constraints: Does not cover s3, gs, file or other non-host schemes. Standard deployments see no change when the storage host matches the default root or artifacts destination. Deployments that store on a second host, or use a workspace default root on another host, must set MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES. Proxied http/https roots under --serve-artifacts are resolved against the local artifacts destination and do not reach this guard. wasbs is not in the host-addressed set.
applies: Server-side acceptance and fetch of artifact locations in mlflow/server/handlers.py and the server-process registry path; not client-side SDK behaviour.
says: Creating an experiment with an SFTP or HDFS storage location returns a 400 error.
Downloading run artifacts fails with an error stating the server cannot connect to location.
Allow tracking servers to connect to secondary storage hosts for experiment and workspace artifacts.
Registering a model version from an external network file path is rejected by server.
Prevent the tracking server from establishing outbound network connections to untrusted remote artifact hosts.
search: The tracking server enforces an artifact host policy in `mlflow/store/artifact/host_policy.py:enforce_server_artifact_uri_host_policy` that restricts host-addressed URIs (such as ftp, sftp, hdfs, http, https, r2, abfss) to the host and port configured in `_MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_ROOT` or `_MLFLOW_SERVER_ARTIFACT_DESTINATION`. Host validation occurs during acceptance in `mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_artifact_uri_scheme` and during repository retrieval via `mlflow/store/artifact/artifact_repository_registry.py:ArtifactRepositoryRegistry.get_artifact_repository` when `is_tracking_server_process()` is true. URIs on other hosts are rejected with HTTP 400 to prevent server-side request forgery (SSRF), unless their scheme is explicitly allowed via `MLFLOW_ALLOWED_HOST_ADDRESSED_ARTIFACT_SCHEMES`. This check does not apply to client-side processes, non-host schemes like s3 or gs, or proxied storage under `--serve-artifacts`.
